mechanism_narrative: A sustained period of low federal funds rates (below 0.5%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.5%, it signals a weak labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 7.5 (i.e., positive returns in > 40% of triggered periods) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When both real GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) are below their 12-month moving averages, it indicates a weakening demand environment that triggers risk-off sentiment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST are below their 12-month moving averages (i.e., positive returns in > 40% of triggered periods) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and annualized CPI > 2.0%), central bank policy becomes restrictive, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.0 and annualized CPI > 2.0 (i.e., positive returns in > 40% of triggered periods) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing activity, which correlates with stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when INDPRO is rising (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When annualized inflation (computed from CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.0%, it signals a need for monetary tightening, which increases risk premiums and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when annualized CPI > 2.0 (i.e., positive returns in > 40% of triggered periods) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When both employment growth (PAYEMS) is below its 12-month moving average and unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 7.5%, it indicates a deteriorating labor market that suppresses consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS < 12mo_avg AND UNRATE > 7.5 (i.e., positive returns in > 40% of triggered periods) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by real GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) both above their 12-month moving averages), the economy is strong but the market is overbought, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when both GDPC1 and HOUST are above their 12-month moving averages (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
